attributes.value: This party would have Fisheries NZ write a report detailing how to quantify environmental harm from different catching methods and then establish a means to adjust conservation levies to match differing environmental impacts and costs. The party would additionally increase fees in a graduated structure to discourage and punish repeat offending.

citations.title: 'Unlocking New Zealand’s Fishing Potential' (PDF), 30 August 2026 (accessed 14 October 2026)

policies.statement: Require Fisheries NZ to write a report that quantifies the economic and environmental cost of fishing methods

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that current focus from Fisheries NZ on the maximum sustainable catch levels is lacking in ambition. The goal should be, according to the party, to grow fishing as both a hobby and an industry. Over time, it says, Fisheries NZ should look to increase catch levels.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would look to progressively manage fish stocks at higher levels than the current maximum-sustainable-catch approach.

citations.title: 'Unlocking New Zealand’s Fishing Potential' (PDF), 30 August 2026 (accessed 14 October 2026)

policies.statement: Seek to progressively increase fish stock levels

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that illegal dumping should be considered another form of vandalism. It says dumping is offensive to those who take pride in their communities.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would increase the infringement fee for illegal dumping from $400 to $1,000, with repeat offenders facing fines of $2,000. For the most serious offences, courts will have the power to impose higher penalties.

citations.title: 'Harsher penalties for trashing communities', 16 October 2026 (accessed 17 October 2026)

policies.statement: Increase penalties for illegal rubbish dumping

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that  average weekly hours for GPs have fallen from 37 to 34 hours a week. That party says that because 35 per cent of GPs intend to retire within five years and 18 per cent are considering moving overseas, NZ needs to make it more attractive for doctors to stay and to recruit from overseas.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would increase funding for doctors' pay to ensure that doctors are paid more and incentivised to take on more appointments and patients. This party estimates that this policy would cost $400 million over four years.

citations.title: 'ACT will invest $400 million to get Kiwis more GP appointments ', 18 October 2026 (accessed 19 October 2026)
'Shorter Waits for your GP', undated (accessed 23 October 2026)

policies.statement: Increase pay for general practice doctors

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that workforce shortages exist in key trade areas. Such professions are viable and positive pathways for many young people who are struggling to find jobs. Aligning education with labour market demands this party says, can be a long-term solution to improving employment outcomes. Additionally, the party argues that trades need to not be considered a second option.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would ensure that funding follows students so that schools receive funding for approved vocational-training programs that are done outside of the student's school. It would create 'Industry Awards' as a qualification equivalent to university entrance. This policy would allow for credits in approved courses to be counted, even after finishing high school.

citations.title: 'ACT will put trades on an equal footing with university', 20 October 2026 (accessed 22 October 2026)

policies.statement: Expand and simplify access to trades for secondary school students

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that parents and their children should have greater school choice. Charter schools can cater to specific needs, such as disability support or special athletic talent.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would set a target of 10,000 student enrolments by the end of 2029, with annual reporting on progress. It would reduce barriers relating to employment, property and funding for state and state-integrated schools to convert to charter schools. It would set a goal to have a charter school in every major town in New Zealand, paired with standards regarding funding and community demand.

citations.title: 'Expanding Charter Schools', undated (accessed 23 October 2026)
'ACT campaigning to transform 10,000 lives', 22 October 2026 (accessed 23 October 2026)

policies.statement: Create a target of 10,000 children attending charter schools by 2029

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that taxpayers are currently funding a helicopter-spraying program. Instead, it says farmers should be allowed to graze their sheep on public conservation land to reduce pests and fire risk. The party claims that in the United States, Australia, and across Europe, targeted grazing is used as a tool for managing invasive plants, controlling vegetation growth, and reducing the risk of wildfires.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would give DOC explicit authority and direction to issue grazing licenses for specified areas of conservation land where grazing can be used effectively, as per an established ecological framework that would identify where grazing is appropriate. Licenses would be conditioned on compliance, and virtual fencing systems would be used to manage stock.

citations.title: 'Grazing to Cut Pests and Fire Risk', undated (accessed 23 October 2026)
'ACT will drive down costs for farmers', 22 October 2026 (accessed 23 October 2026)

policies.statement: Allow more sheep to graze on conservation land

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that it wishes to expand accessibility and scope of permitting for agriculture. The party claims this can help promote growth and lower costs associated with regulatory compliance.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would introduce ten new permitting standards relating to farm plans, vegetable growing, on-farm water storage, gravel extraction, drain maintenance, effluent management, fertiliser application, farm quarries, wetland restoration, and small-and-medium-scale solar. It would additionally guarantee flexible land use, so farmers won’t require a resource consent when expanding into new markets if they remain compliant with national standards.

citations.title: 'ACT will drive down costs for farmers', 22 October 2026 (accessed 23 October 2026)

policies.statement: Introduce new permitting standards for agriculture

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that private property rights are important to incentivise investment and to protect livelihoods. Councils can, through their policies regarding Significant Natural Areas or Outstanding Natural Landscapes, undermine property values and thus the investments of farmers.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would would require councils to pay 'fair' compensation if decisions made by such councils interfere with agricultural industry and farming.

citations.title: 'ACT will drive down costs for farmers', 22 October 2026 (accessed 23 October 2026)

policies.statement: Require compensation for individuals if council decisions affect private land

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that rural workforce visas are seasonal, such as the Global Workforce Seasonal Visa and the Peak Seasonal Visa. The party says a year-round visa needs to be introduced to ensure labour demands are met.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would create a standalone, three-year visa specifically for dairy, sheep and beef, and general farm work. Would be tied to industry, not location or employer. The visa would be for 3 years, if no suitable New Zealander is available, the visa is reissued for a further three years. The party would additionally add a new agricultural stream to the Work to Residence Visa.

citations.title: 'A Rural Workforce Visa', undated (accessed 24 October 2026)

policies.statement: Create a rural workforce visa

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that it could potentially be cheaper for consumers to buy an animal directly from a producer, rather than once it has been processed by a butcher. It says buying and processing home kill should be easier. It says that currently, home-killed meat can only be eaten the animal owner, their family or household, and farm employees and that the rules haven't been updated in twenty years.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would revise regulations around selling and purchasing home-kill meat.

citations.title: 'Cutting red tape between the farm gate and the freezer', 31 August 2026 (accessed 26 October 2026)
'ACT will make farming fun again ', 20 September 2026 (accessed 21 September 2026)
'ACT will drive down costs for farmers', 22 October 2026 (accessed 23 October 2026)

policies.statement: Reduce regulations related to selling home-kill meat

partyAffiliation.candidacyDescription: Candidate for the Wellington Bays electorate

attributes.name: Why I'm standing
attributes.value: New Zealand should be one of the most prosperous countries on Earth, but we're not meeting our potential. My wife and I have ten grandchildren between us, and I want them to inherit a country that rewards hard work, values freedom, and gives people the opportunity to build better lives. I'm running because I'm not prepared to sit back while New Zealand becomes poorer, less ambitious, and weighed down by ever-bigger government. Party vote ACT.

attributes.name: About me
attributes.value: I've spent decades asking difficult questions, challenging people in power, and saying what I think. I'll bring energy and common-sense to Parliament. I'm standing list-only. The best way to elect me and more of ACT's strong team is to party vote ACT. It'll keep the coalition Government in power, but going further and faster on the issues that matter most. This election is crucial, a lurch to the left would devastate our economy for generations.

I'm asking you to vote for whichever electorate candidate you believe will best represent your area and to give your party vote to ACT.

attributes.value: I'm a current Councillor, standing up against undemocratic co-governance arrangements. I've experienced the issues in councils that drive rates up while the services you receive in return aren't up to scratch. I'm standing list-only, so the best way to elect me and more of ACT's strong team is to party vote ACT: to Lock Labour Out, re-elect the coalition Government, and give ACT the strength to go further and faster in unlocking New Zealand's potential.
